reason: E1 confirms the low yield strength of FCC HEAs, but neither E1 nor E2 provides any evidence for the proposed gradient dual-phase microstructure, the specific processing route, or the activation of TRIP and twinning in such a structure. The cited evidence only supports the baseline material property, leaving the key mechanistic and processing premises entirely unsupported.
premises: FCC HEAs like CrMnFeCoNi have high ductility but low yield strength (~350 MPa)
Severe cold rolling (~70% reduction) can create a deformed surface layer
Short gradient annealing at 800°C can produce a dual-phase structure with a metastable surface and undeformed core
The metastable surface layer will undergo TRIP (transformation-induced plasticity) under load
Deformation twinning will be activated in the gradient structure to enhance plasticity
